newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids flat in thin, post-Easter activity.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids flat in thin, post-Easter activity.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished mostly unchanged against Thursday's level on the last day of March in thin, post-Easter activity.
Resid prices were little moved by further restriction of vessel traffic on the Mississippi River after a barge carrying toxic petrochemicals capsized March 17.

Last Friday, the Coast Guard ruled that tank vessels or tank ships with 1,600 gross tons or more carrying certain petroleum products or chemicals, as well as deep-draft chemical tank ships, must travel in daylight hours only downward between Baton Rouge and New Orleans.
Spot values for high sulphur, bunker material in the U.S. Gulf remained pressured by easing interest and more offers reportedly from the Caribbean and South America.
"The bunker (supply) is overpriced right now," said one physical resid dealer.

USG three percent sulphur grade widened to $13.75-14.25 a barrel from $14.00-14.25 Thursday. USG three percent paper edged down 25 cents from Thursday to $13.25-50. One percent physical was still thinly discussed at $14.75-15.00.
In the New York harbor, one percent physical slipped to $15.50-16.00 from $15.75-16.25 Thursday. One percent NYH paper for April was firmer at $15.20-35, up from Thursday's $15.05-15.15.
NYH HSFO prices finished steady against Thursday with three percent staying at $13.50-75.
NYMEX May crude futures resumed its recent skid after Friday's rebound, settling down 29 cents at $20.41 a barrel.

Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate for April 1 delivery jumped near $2.40 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $15.12 a barrel equivalent, higher than Wednesday's $2.17-2.22/mmBtu or $13.86/bbl equivalent for delivery today.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, continued to hover at $1.84/mmBtu or $11.59/bbl equivalent.
